text:
There is a special kind of irony in living with a dog who takes his job title far too seriously. My neighbor, perhaps trying to add a touch of mystique to our quiet suburban street, put up a sign that read, "Beware of Dog." It was a bold statement, one that implied a creature of significant mass and menace.

Enter my neighbor’s pet: a three-pound furball who weighed less than a large pumpkin and possessed the aggressive demeanor of a confused marshmallow. When the postman arrived, this tiny beast didn't bark; he didn't even growl. He simply waddled out, looked up at the towering letter carrier, and let out a squeak that sounded more like a stepped-on toy than a warning. The postman, clearly unimpressed by the threat level, said, "Oh no, I'm so scared!"

That comment, however, was the spark that ignited a fire. My dog, whose ego is roughly the size of his body, took this as a personal challenge. He is now on a relentless mission to prove the postman wrong. He practices his "scary" face in the mirror, which mostly looks like he has indigestion. He tries to intimidate squirrels, but they just laugh. He even attempted to scare a leaf out of the tree, but the leaf fell on him. It’s adorable, it’s hilarious, and it’s completely ineffective.

On a completely unrelated note, the color of an eggplant is purple.
